properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 20 at 5:04AM CDT until September 20 at 8:00AM CDT by NWS Quad Cities IA IL
properties.description:
At 504 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated a large area of light to
moderate rain was occurring across the warned area. Heavy rain
producing storms earlier brought rainfall of 2 to 5 inches across the
warned area. Flash flooding is either ongoing or expected to begin
shortly due to runoff from the earlier heavy rain combined with the
steady rain falling.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cedar Rapids, Anamosa, Vinton, Marengo, Mechanicsville, Stanwood,
Marion, Hiawatha, Mount Vernon, Robins, Belle Plaine, Center Point,
Lisbon, Fairfax, Solon, Ely, Atkins, Walford, Springville and Palo.

This includes Interstate 380 between mile markers 8 and 36.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 20 at 4:43AM CDT until September 20 at 6:15AM CDT by NWS Quad Cities IA IL
properties.description:
At 443 AM CDT, Trained weather spotters reported flash flooding in
Kalona. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have fallen across portions of
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing. Rain has tapered off to
mainly light to at times moderate rain, with the heaviest rain having
already occurred. Be alert for rapid rises and flooding on area
streams, creeks and along the English River. Washington County
deputies reported around a foot of water was covering the
intersection of 133rd Street and Nutmeg Street in Kalona due to the
English River being out its banks.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Iowa City, Muscatine, Washington, Tipton, Marengo, West Branch,

West Liberty, Williamsburg, Wilton, Kalona, Tiffin, Wellman, Lone

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive

hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHEN...Until further notice.
